question.problem: Calculate $\int \frac{5}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $u=3x+4.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{5}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary positive constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+C & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{5}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3x+4|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{5}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x=\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3x+4|).
$$
